whatTheyArgued: In his 263 CE commentary on the Jiuzhang suanshu (Nine Chapters), Liu Hui explains why the book's bare algorithms work. For the circle (problem 1.32, area = half circumference x half diameter) he inscribes a hexagon and doubles the sides (12-gon, 24-gon...), claims the leftover shrinks until 'no more cut is possible' and the polygon coincides with the circle, and concludes the area formula (Mikami 1913 translation, verbatim snip; Siu 1993 summarizes the same three steps). He also corrects the book's implicit pi = 3, saying it is only the ratio for the inscribed hexagon. What I read does not show him laying down axioms or a rule that results 'not derived from premises do not count'.

scholarship.ref: Man-Keung Siu, 'Proof and Pedagogy in Ancient China: Examples from Liu Hui's Commentary on Jiu Zhang Suan Shu', Educational Studies in Mathematics 24 (1993), 345-357 (full text read)
scholarship.supports: the circle-area commentary in three steps (polygon doubling, limit claim with sandwich, conclusion); Liu Hui's remark that pi = 3 is only the hexagon ratio
scholarship.disputes: Siu notes that if 'proof' means deductive demonstration from stated definitions and postulates, ancient Chinese mathematics has none (Szabo's view); if it means an explanation that convinces and enlightens, Liu Hui supplies many. Which sense applies is the dispute. This reading is Siu's; I did not read competing scholars (e.g. Chemla, Guo Shuchun) in full.

ourUse: derivation.js (floor 6): a corroborated note becomes a PREMISE; licensed composition derives products that land with no witnesses, only premises and provenance to bytes; conceding a premise withdraws every product resting on it transitively. Handle comment: 'after the mathematician who proved each step from results already established; what isn't derived from a premise doesn't count'.

bends.ours: A derived note counts only if it rests on corroborated premises on the ledger; a hard wall (no witnesses, withdrawn when a premise is conceded).
bends.theirs: Liu Hui's commentary justifies existing algorithms by explanation and geometric argument (polygon doubling plus a limit claim). Siu stresses it is not axiomatic deduction. The 'premise or it does not count' wall is our design, and the corroboration/withdrawal ledger has no counterpart in the text read.

bends.ours: Compendium work/credit: 'a derived result rests on established premises or it does not count' and 'gave geometry its rigour'.
bends.theirs: Not a statement Liu Hui makes in the passage snipped; 'rigour' is our gloss and, per Siu, contested as a description of his proofs.

bends.ours: One verified snip (circle area by exhaustion) stands for a general doctrine of derivation.
bends.theirs: The snip shows a limiting argument for one formula. It does not state a general epistemic rule.

bends.ours: organ header comment opens with a first-person 'speaks' block and commentary in the archon's voice ('My teaching prioritizes...', 'I believe...'), generated text presented as the author's own words (derivation.js opening block: 'My teaching prioritizes the clarity and precision of the derivation process...').
bends.theirs: Liu Hui wrote nothing of the kind; only the quoted commentary lines are his (in Mikami's translation).
